paper.title_en: Insight–HXMT observations of the 2025–2026 outburst of GS 1354 - 64: distinct disk flux–temperature tracks during the state evolution
paper.abstract_en: We report Insight–HXMT observations of the 2025–2026 outburst from the black hole X-ray binary GS 1354 - 64, complemented by MAXI monitoring. Unlike the previous hard-only outbursts of this source, the 2025–2026 event reached a much higher intensity, rose slowly, and was accompanied by multiple prominent X-ray flares.In the hardness–intensity diagram, the source evolved from the hard state to the intermediate state, and continued toward softer states. Broadband spectral analysis shows two distinct disk flux–temperature tracks: Track 1 follows <math altimg="si10.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∝</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0.61</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.04</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>, whereas Track 2 follows <math altimg="si11.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∝</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4.69</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.14</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>, suggesting a change in the radiative coupling between the disk and corona. The After Flares observations at MJD  ≥ 61098 follow <math altimg="si12.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∝</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3.83</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.27</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>, consistent within uncertainties with the standard F∝T<sup loc="post">4</sup> expectation, while the MJD  ≥ 61098 diskbb normalizations are described by a characteristic normalization with measurable intrinsic scatter. Under the assumption that the apparent inner radius corresponding to this characteristic normalization is identified with the ISCO, we obtain tentative constraints of D ≳ 2.18 kpc and 47.7<sup loc="post">∘</sup> ≲ i ≲ 79<sup loc="post">∘</sup>. For a black hole mass of 10 M⊙, the peak unabsorbed 0.1–100 keV luminosity is approximately (1.3–4.7)% LEdd for distances of 2.18–4.1 kpc.
